quote: I don't know. I would I you know, I would just wanted to look into it.
stewart_read: The customer hands the rep a thin, non-committal reason for interest with an unrelated political aside. The rep should have gently probed (e.g., what prompted the look-into-it, bill pain, a neighbor, an ad) but instead accepted the vague answer at 01:15 and moved on.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged further probing as unproductive given the rambling, off-topic answer — a reasonable read given the customer's disengagement, but the schema treats depth here as the emotional anchor for the whole call, so the miss still counts.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to ask one clarifying follow-up before moving past the interest question, even on a low-energy customer — a thin anchor here means nothing to flip on later.

quote: to qualify for those, you just need to have a form of taxable income and a credit score of six fifty or higher.
stewart_read: The schema's documented credit threshold is 670, but the rep states 650 — the same drift already flagged once in the schema (SESSION18_fcbf33c1, Meg). This is now a second data point suggesting either the rep is consistently wrong or policy actually differs from the schema.
coaching_implication: Flag to management as a schema_drift_detection item: two independent reps stating 650, not 670. Needs Kenny's reconciliation before coaching individual reps on 'wrong' numbers.

quote: just to qualify for the new furnace.
stewart_read: The rep says 'new furnace' when discussing solar tax credit qualification — almost certainly a script slip-up or leftover phrasing from a different offer/vertical, immediately followed by rep re-reading the qualifier without correcting the error.
coaching_implication: Point out the literal misstatement to the rep — even if the customer didn't catch it, this kind of script bleed-through undermines legitimacy on a call already trending suspicious.

quote: And why do you need this information?
stewart_read: This is a trust/privacy pushback tied to the credit and income question. The rep's response ('Just to see if you qualify for the incentives') validates the ask on the company's terms rather than reframing why this information benefits the CUSTOMER (e.g., tying it back to whatever bill pain or motivation she might have, however thin).
alternative_hypothesis: This could be read as a legitimate procedural answer rather than an objection to invert — but the customer's tone and follow-up at 03:16 confirm it functioned as a trust objection, not a simple clarifying question.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep on reframing qualifier questions in terms of customer benefit ('this just helps us make sure any program we show you is one you'd actually qualify for') rather than restating the company's internal need for the data.

quote: I just don't like giving out personal information to a person that calls me on the phone.
stewart_read: This is the same trust concern escalating into an explicit statement. The rep repeats the identical reassurance used at 02:44 instead of trying a new angle — no acknowledgment of the specific fear (giving info to a phone caller), no legitimacy-building move (e.g., referencing the form she filled out, or offering to verify identity another way).
coaching_implication: This is the clearest single moment to replay with the rep: same objection, same rep line repeated almost verbatim, zero adaptation. Direct evidence for multi_angle_resilience coaching.

quote: No. I don't wanna do this. I I don't wanna do this. I don't wanna just be giving out information.
stewart_read: The customer states a clear boundary twice in one breath — this is a distress signal, not a negotiating position. The rep's response ('Well, I mean, yeah, like I said,') cut off by the transcript ending suggests the rep was continuing to defend the ask rather than de-escalating or backing off.
coaching_implication: Coach on recognizing when a customer's repeated refusal signals the call should end gracefully (thank them, offer to follow up if they reconsider) rather than continuing to press the same justification.
